title: Five Faces

source.quote: Positive Nurturing Parent implies caring which is provided from a position of genuine regard for the person helped.

setting: Wednesday, 9pm. Sam, a developer, is still online, fourth night this week, deep in the deploy channel.

L1.line: Don't worry about any of this - I'll just handle the deploy myself, you go home and rest.
cues: takes the task without asking first
L1.question: Which functional ego state is Priti showing here - and which side of it?

options.feedback: Close, but check whether Sam was asked or just overridden - true positive Nurturing Parent offers care without taking the choice away from the other person.
Right. The smile is warm, but she's already taken the keyboard - that one-up "I'll decide what's best for you" move is the textbook smother-mother, not genuine care.

options.text: Positive Controlling Parent - a firm, protective boundary
options.feedback: There's no boundary being set here, no rule, no limit - Priti isn't controlling anything, she's taking over the caretaking entirely.
There's no judgment or command here, no "you should" - this is phrased as help, which is exactly what makes it Nurturing, not Controlling.

L1.lesson: Nurturing Parent isn't automatically the good one: when care removes someone else's choice or decides what's best for them without asking, it discounts them just as much as a put-down does - that's negative Nurturing Parent, and it can look kinder than a boundary that is actually healthier.

L2.intro: Priti means well, but taking over isn't going to fix the pattern. You're Sam's manager - what do you say?

beats.line: Priti's right, it's fine, I'll just push through tonight too.
cues: already turning back to the screen

options.text: Priti's got it tonight. You're off the rotation for the next two nights - no exceptions.
options.outcome: Sam blinks, then exhales. "Okay... thanks, actually." The rule holds without a lecture.
options.lesson: Positive Controlling Parent sets a real limit aimed at Sam's wellbeing, stated plainly, without a put-down - that's the boundary Priti's smothering never actually offered.

options.text: Don't worry about it, I'll just quietly move your tickets to someone else.
options.outcome: Sam doesn't even notice the tickets move until Friday, and never learns why his week got lighter.
options.lesson: This fixes the symptom without naming it, and decides for Sam instead of with him - gentler than Priti's move, but the same one-up shape underneath.

options.text: You should really learn to pace yourself better.
options.outcome: Sam's shoulders drop further. "Yeah... I know." Nothing changes, he just feels worse about it.
options.lesson: This sounds like a boundary but it's actually a judgment with no limit attached - negative Controlling Parent discounts Sam instead of protecting him.

options.text: How many nights is this now - what's actually going on with the deploy?
options.outcome: Sam pauses. "Honestly, no one's owned the rollback plan since Deep left." Useful, but tonight's exhaustion is still unresolved.
options.lesson: Good Adult diagnosis of the root cause, worth following up on - but it leaves tonight unaddressed; sometimes an Adult finding still needs a Controlling Parent boundary attached to actually take effect.

fields.label: Draw the vectors for Priti's offer, and for Rhea's best response.
In under 60 words: why is Priti's "I'll handle it, you go home" not the same as Rhea's "you're off rotation for two nights"?

echo.setting: 48 hours later: Rhea's own mother calls and offers to "just come over and sort out" Rhea's kitchen renovation.
echo.line: Don't worry about any of it, I'll handle the contractor myself.
echo.shape: same CP+/NP- diagnose shape as L1
